title: Playground
lede: Try a rule on made-up data and see what the engine saw. Nothing here is published or saved to HQ; an experiment you save stays in this browser.
copied: A copy of rule {{id}}, with example data. Nothing you do here changes the rule.

kind.label: Kind
kind.hint: Switching the kind starts its example rule and data.

asOf.label: As of
asOf.hint: The moment the engine evaluates at, in local time.

access.deniedTitle: You do not have access to the playground
access.deniedHint: The playground needs the rule playground grant. Ask HQ to grant it.

data.title: Data
data.hint: The request, patient and lines the engine reads, as JSON.
data.rawHint: Any text, sent as it is, even when it is not valid JSON. The outcome lists what the engine read, ignored and refused.
data.formHint: The whole dataset as a form: request, patient, lines, history, reference rows and eligibility facts (and the payer, for coverage). An edit shows in the JSON at once, and the other way round.

form.more: The JSON holds more than the form shows. These keys are kept as they are; edit them on the JSON tab:

problem.invalid: The data is not one valid JSON object, so the form cannot show it. Fix it on the JSON tab.
problem.unshaped: The data has a shape the form cannot hold (a request or patient that is not an object, or lines that are not a list of objects). Edit it on the JSON tab.

form.referenceHint: SFDA and CHI rows the reference conditions read, instead of the live editions.
form.referenceNone: None — the reference conditions find no row.
form.refFieldsHint: An edited value keeps the type it had (a number, a list of codes); a new one is text.
form.eligibilityHint: Facts of the payer's eligibility answer; they belong to the whole request.
form.eligibilityNone: None — every eligibility fact is unknown.
form.payerHint: What the payer stated, per deductible group (coverage experiments only).

flatten.title: Flatten a payer's answer
flatten.hint: Paste a payer's raw eligibility answer to see the facts HQ reads from it. Nothing is sent to the payer.
flatten.responseHint: One JSON object, as the payer sent it.
flatten.invalid: The payer's answer is not valid JSON, so nothing was sent. It must be one JSON object.
flatten.failed: The playground could not flatten this answer.
flatten.denied: You have no access to the playground.
flatten.none: The answer holds no eligibility fact.
flatten.useHint: Replaces every eligibility fact of the experiment with these. An edit you make afterwards is kept.
flatten.used: These are now the experiment's eligibility facts.
flatten.dataInvalid: The data is not valid JSON, so the facts cannot be put in it.

rule.title: Rule
rule.hint: A scratch ruleset of one or more rules, as JSON in the engine's spelling.
rule.hintEditors: A scratch ruleset of one or more rules, built with the editors of the kind's own rule screen. The engine JSON under them follows every edit, and an edit to the JSON moves the editors once it parses.

problem.data: The data is not valid JSON, so nothing was sent. It must be one JSON object.
problem.document: The rule is not valid JSON, so nothing was sent. It must be one JSON object.

outcome.title: Outcome
outcome.empty: The outcome appears here shortly after an edit.
outcome.failed: The playground could not run this experiment.

tabs.label: Outcome views
tabs.live: What the live check would say

outcome.nothingMatched: Nothing matched: no line met a rule's whole condition.

errors.title: The engine could not read the rule
errors.onBlocks: Shown on their block in the Rule pane: {{n}}

intake.title: What the engine took from the raw text
intake.hint: A key the engine does not know is ignored; a value of the wrong type is refused.

trace.empty: The engine read no block on this line.

reads.title: What the engine read
reads.none: The door sent no read log for this run, so the explanation reads from the trace alone.
reads.lineNone: The engine read no fact on this line.
reads.wholeRequestHint: An eligibility fact belongs to the whole request: the same value on every line.
reads.noLiveSource: No live source: reads unknown at the till

explain.title: Explain this result
explain.matched: On line {{line}}, rule {{rule}} matched: every block held.
explain.false: On line {{line}}, rule {{rule}} did not match because block {{block}} was false.
explain.unknown: On line {{line}}, rule {{rule}} did not match because block {{block}} was unknown.
explain.missing: It was unknown because {{path}} was missing.
explain.unparsed: It was unknown because {{path}} read {{raw}}, which did not parse.

unparsedAs.number: It was unknown because {{path}} read {{raw}}, which is not a number.
unparsedAs.date: It was unknown because {{path}} read {{raw}}, which is not a date.
unparsedAs.flag: It was unknown because {{path}} read {{raw}}, which is not a yes or no.
unparsedAs.text: It was unknown because {{path}} read {{raw}}, which is not text.

explain.nothingMatched: No line met a rule’s whole condition.
explain.noLines: The data had no lines, so the engine read nothing.
explain.lineNoTrace: On line {{line}}, the engine read no block.
explain.noReads: The door sent no read log, so this explanation reads from the trace alone.

verdict.none: The live check said nothing for this experiment.

experiments.name: Experiment name
experiments.renameHint: Renames the picked experiment to the name in the box.

said.imported: Imported {{name}}. It is not kept in this browser until you save it.
said.off: Storage is off in this browser, so experiments cannot be kept here. Export and import still work.
said.notReady: Fix the JSON first: an experiment that does not parse cannot be saved or exported.
said.taken: Another saved experiment is already called {{name}}.
said.missing: That saved experiment is no longer here.

refused.title: The file was not imported
refused.malformed: The file is not valid JSON. Nothing was loaded.
refused.notExperiment: The file is not a playground experiment. Nothing was loaded.
refused.noVersion: The file does not say which version it is. Nothing was loaded.
refused.unknownVersion: The file's version is not one this playground knows. Nothing was loaded.
refused.newerVersion: The file was made by a newer playground. Nothing was loaded.
refused.invalid: The file's experiment is incomplete or has a wrong value. Nothing was loaded.
refused.fileFailed: The file could not be read.

lessons.label: Lessons
lessons.hint: A lesson loads a ready experiment that teaches one idea. It replaces the current experiment. Edit it freely: Check says whether the outcome still meets the lesson.
lessons.checkHint: Compares the latest answer with what the lesson expects.
lessons.met: Met: the outcome is what the lesson expects.

diff.matched: Matched lines: expected {{want}}, the answer has {{got}}.
diff.trace: Line {{line}}, rule {{ruleId}}, block {{blockPath}}: expected {{want}}, the answer has {{got}}.
diff.verdictRule: Line {{line}}, {{field}}: expected it set by rule {{want}}, the answer has rule {{got}}.
diff.ignoredMissing: Raw key {{path}}: expected it ignored, but the answer does not list it.
diff.ignoredHint: Raw key {{path}}: expected the near-miss {{want}}, the answer has {{got}}.

unknownVsFalse.title: 1. Unknown is not false
unknownVsFalse.explain: Line 1 has no days of supply, so the block <c>daysSupply above 90</c> reads unknown: the engine cannot say. Line 2 has 30 days, so the same block reads false. Neither line matches, but for different reasons, and a rule's <c>onUnknown</c> decides what an unknown does at the till. Try giving line 1 a days supply of 120.

groups.title: 2. Groups: any, all and not
groups.explain: The first block is an "any" group: it holds because the days supply is above 90, even though the quantity is not 5 or more (its second condition reads false). The second block is a "not": the price is not above 1,000, so it holds. The third is an "all" group: every condition in it must hold. Change the quantity to 12 and watch the "all" group fail.

quantityCap.title: 3. A quantity cap
quantityCap.explain: A coverage rule caps the quantity at one pack when the supply is longer than 90 days. On the live-check tab, line 1 (120 days) shows the cap 1, set by rule C-1. Line 2 (30 days) has no cap: the rule does not hold there and the payer states none.

categoryOrder.title: 4. Category order: who wins
categoryOrder.explain: Category rules run in order, and the first that holds sets the category. On line 1 only K-2 holds (a price of 50 is not above 100), so it is G2. On line 2 both hold and K-1 comes first, so it is G1. Swap the two rules to see the winner change.

historyWindow.title: 5. A history window
historyWindow.explain: The history holds one dispense of the same item on <c>2026-10-20</c>. As of <c>2026-10-30</c> that is 10 days back, inside the 30-day window, so the block holds. Move "as of" to <c>2026-11-25</c>: the dispense falls outside the window and the block reads false.

benefit66.title: 6. Benefit category 66, field by field
benefit66.explain: The payer's answer for benefit category 66 carries four numbers: <c>benefit</c> 50,000, <c>approvalLimit</c> 10,000, <c>copayPct</c> 20 and <c>copayMax</c> 75. One rule per field asks whether it holds exactly 10,000, and only <c>approvalLimit</c> does. So a "limit of 10,000" is the approval limit, the amount above which the payer wants prior approval: not the benefit, and not the copay cap.

otherPayer.title: 7. The same benefit code at another payer
otherPayer.explain: Benefit codes belong to the payer. This experiment reads <c>benefit[66].approvalLimit</c> again, but the request is at payer <c>0001100099</c>, whose category 66 has an approval limit of 100. The price of 120.5 is above it, so the guard warns, where at the first payer's 10,000 it would not. What each payer's code means is kept in insurer settings, never assumed.

crossLine.title: 8. A check across lines
crossLine.explain: A formula can read every line of the request through <c>$request.lines</c>. Here <c>lines(filter($request.lines, $line.item == '200021'))</c> counts the lines of SKU 200021. There are two, so the formula holds on every line, and the first block keeps the warning to the 200021 lines: lines 1 and 3 match, line 2 does not. Remove line 3 and nothing matches.

rawNearMiss.title: 9. A Raw near-miss
rawNearMiss.explain: Raw text is sent as it is, and the engine reads only the keys it knows. This line says <c>qty</c>, not <c>quantity</c>, so the intake report lists it as ignored with its near-miss, and the rule's quantity block reads unknown. Rename the key and the line matches.

compare.title: Compare A/B
compare.hint: B started as a copy of this experiment (A). Edit B's data or rule here; the kind and "as of" are A's. Both run, and what differs is highlighted. Leaving Compare keeps A.
compare.waiting: The comparison appears once A and B both have an outcome.
compare.same: A and B give the same outcome.
compare.differs: A and B differ. What differs is highlighted.
compare.verdict: What the live check would say

ruleset.label: The rules, in the order the engine runs them
ruleset.jsonOnly: The editors cannot show this rule, so edit it in the JSON below. It still runs.
ruleset.broken: The JSON does not parse, so the editors show the last rules that did. Fix the JSON to edit them again.
ruleset.empty: No rules yet. Add one, or write them in the JSON.
